key_insight: Band-avoiding occupation-constrained DFT (ba-occ-DFT) can compute defect energetics reliably even when standard DFT predicts a zero band gap.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to predict defect charge-transition levels in narrow-gap semiconductors such as InAs, improving defect-aware materials design.
method: Constrain electronic occupations to avoid spurious filling of band-edge states.
Separate band-edge errors from defect-level energetics in total-energy calculations.
Apply the approach to InAs, a narrow-gap case where the DFT gap collapses to zero.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that ba-occ-DFT yields rigorous defect level predictions for InAs despite a zero DFT band gap.
watch_item: The method depends on correctly identifying and constraining band-edge states, which may require careful implementation for complex defect structures.
paper_title: No band gap, no problem: Defects in InAs using a band-avoiding occupation-constrained density functional theory
